%doc: Editorial corrections applied on top of the ARK Starmap mirror to produce Module:SystemMap/systems.json. Everything here is a judgement the upstream data cannot supply: which article a body links to, where a belt sits between planets, which planet is really a moon. Run `mise run systemmap` after editing. Keys are the system name, then `page`, `star`, `companion`, `companionShape` and/or `bodies`. Under `bodies` the key is the upstream body name (or its designation, when upstream gives it no name, which is what the rail labels it anyway); where two bodies in one system share that key, each is addressed by the type-qualified form instead, such as `Ellis XI (PLANET)`, and the generator's error names both. Supported per-body keys: page, label, icon, iconRatio, after, moonOf, km. `star` and `companion` take the same keys except after and moonOf, which a body nothing on the rail orbits has no use for; their km is a radius. `page` corrects the system's own article, which is otherwise "<upstream name> system". `companionShape` overrides how a second star is drawn — `nested` where it orbits the primary, `paired` where the two co-orbit — and should be left to the derivation from upstream's parent_id. `exclude` accepts either key form. A body listed here that no longer exists upstream FAILS the generator rather than being ignored, because a silently-dropped correction is exactly how this work gets lost across a refetch; the same is true of a `star` block on a system upstream files no star for, and of a `companion` block on a system with one star. Listing a system here is what puts it in systems.json, in this order; an empty entry means nothing needed correcting. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-system-map-rollout-design.md.
